newsitem.title: USA: FY97 sugar quota has no price effect-USDA Glickman.
newsitem.headline: FY97 sugar quota has no price effect-USDA Glickman.

text.p: Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said Friday he did not expect the U.S. sugar quota of 2.3 million tonnes to have a major effect on prices.
"I think it's not going to have a dramatic effect on prices at all," Glickman told reporters. "In fact, as I said, the domestic market today is relatively unchanged."

Earlier, USDA set the fiscal 1997 import quota at 2.3 million tonnes with 1.7 million to be allocated Monday. The rest would be reviewed later for release under a formula based on the projected stocks to use ratio.
"We've made it basically a one-year pilot program," Glickman said of the formula. "We'll see how it works."
The formula which will be used during reviews set for January, March and May represented an attempt to introduce stability in sugar marketing, Glickman said.
Glickman also pointed to areas where USDA altered quota to alleviate concerns among domestic growers. Chief change was to reduce the quota, which was proposed for 2.475 million tonnes.
